ALEX, and he is right: codegen blindness is a SPEC/REFINE fail. SpecOps should deliver the context, not just a spec.

Today a refined ticket hands the builder ~700 chars of SPEC.md and nothing else. The builder then invents a worker from a title. That is the 500s.

CONTEXT PACK requirement — refine output is not done until it contains:
1. The TARGET FILES — actual current source of the files to be edited, fetched at refine time (repo + path already known per gate-3 binding).
2. Repo layout one-pager — what exists, entry points, deploy target.
3. Prior attempt errors — the raw block reasons from earlier attempts on this ticket, so a retry knows what failed.
4. The contract assertions it must pass.

And codegen consumes the pack: EDIT tickets prompt = existing file + spec + errors → patch out, not fresh worker. Retry loop feeds the deploy error back once before blocking.

That makes 2313 (EDIT lane) + context pack one change in the refine drain that just landed — refineStep already runs, it now assembles the pack instead of only SPEC.md.

Route: loop refines and builds it — it can now. GLM review (m2974) should cover this too: is the pack sufficient, what is missing.
